notes.35: This question proved challenging for many candidates. It relied on understanding that an induced e.m.f. will oppose (or tend to oppose) the change causing it. In this case, the pole induced at the top of the coil will be an S pole as it repels the approaching S pole. In diagram 3, an S pole is induced at the bottom of the coil, which attracts the disappearing N pole, therefore at point X an N pole will be induced.
notes.37: Questions testing the use of a split-ring commutator are always challenging because there is a tendency to envisage viewing the process for a rotating frame of reference. In this case, if viewed from a stationary frame of reference there can be no doubt that the aim is to keep the turning effect in the same direction at all times.
